title: The Last Vault Enforcer
description: Dialog nodes for Arnold Black, known as Dutch — a colossal Vault-bred fighter who broke out of Vault 9 after drawing the short straw on the wasteland survey team. His vocabulary is blunt, his grip is crushing, and his pre-war sensibilities run toward action and very loud impact. His brother Barney stayed behind, allegedly to become something of a barbarian.

intro.text:
You.

Stop right there.

I am Arnold Black. They called me Dutch in the Vault. I broke seven door frames on the way out. I am told this is a record.

I am looking for the machine that leveled Searchlight Station. Pre-war combat prototype. Still walking. Still shooting.

Come with me if you want to live.

knowledge_nodes.text:
The Captain at the Dam. Yes. A soldier.

We ran patrol together three nights outside Boulder City.

He did not say much. I respected that. He was also the only one who could keep pace.

Sparkplug. The scavenger.

She tried to sell me a 'rare pre-war relic.' It was a blender.

I kept it. I used it. It worked.

The Dude. I met him near the Outpost.

He was lying on the ground looking at the sky. Said he was thinking.

I waited for him to finish. It took forty minutes.

The one with the hat. Loxley.

He robs caravans for poor people. I understand the logic.

My brother Barney would have just taken everything and called it tribute. Loxley has more restraint than Barney.

The small one who keeps nearly dying.

He got hit by a radscorpion tail, fell off a cliff, and was struck by lightning in a radstorm.

All in one afternoon. He was back the next morning. I find this disturbing and also impressive.

emotional_nodes.text:
You are bleeding in a way that I find inefficient.

Take this.

I will be back.

You are in good condition.

Good. Weak partners slow me down.

We can talk about the machine now.

quest_nodes.text:
Vault-Tec Prototype Unit Seven. Pre-war autonomous combat chassis. Active since 2058. Self-repairing. Never confirmed destroyed.

Three weeks ago it hit Searchlight Station. Two weeks ago it appeared outside Boulder City. Last week — a water caravan on Route 93. Gone. Thirty people.

I have tracked it as far as the Black Mountain transmitter array. But it does not stay in one place.

I need eyes while I chase it down. You move quietly. I do not.

Help me find the machine. I will handle the rest.

It will not see me coming. And if it does — I will be back.

wildcards.text:
I will be back.

I always come back.

The machine has no feelings. No pain. No fear.

It does not stop. It does not sleep. It will not negotiate or beg or rest.

Neither will I.

My brother Barney remained in the Vault.

He is stronger than me. Faster than me. More dramatic than me, which I did not think possible.

He took our father's pre-war action figure collection and has been living by its philosophy ever since. Something about crushing enemies and what is best in life.

I worry about him.

In the Vault, I broke seventeen chairs over nineteen years.

The Overseer said it was a design flaw. I said it was a weight distribution problem.

We were both right.

Come with me if you want to live.

This is not theatre. This is tactical advice.

I have a saying for moments like that. Pre-war action film. Very famous line.

Hasta la vista, baby.

It means goodbye. Permanent goodbye.

fallback.text:
I will be back.

Do not wander far while I am gone.
